title: Stream & bulk embeddings ingestion: batch API + async jobs + idempotency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers need to upload large embedding payloads (tens of thousands to millions of items) and/or continuous streams of records from pipelines. The current single-request embeddings endpoint times out or is inefficient for large-scale ingestion and offers poor retry semantics. Goal: provide a robust set of ingestion primitives: a synchronous bulk/batch endpoint for medium-sized uploads, an async job API for very large bulk ingestion, and a streaming/append interface for pipeline use-cases. Important properties: efficient GPU batching at the runtime layer, end-to-end idempotency to avoid double-indexing/charging on retries, clear partial-success semantics, and observability for job progress and failures.
acceptance_criteria: Add /v1/embeddings/batch endpoint that accepts up to 10k records in a single request and returns per-item statuses within 2s median for small models
Design and implement /v1/embeddings/async to create ingestion jobs that return a job_id and support chunked uploads and resumable parts
Job state machine persisted: queued -> running -> partial_success -> failed -> completed. Jobs must be durable across control-plane restarts
Idempotency: clients can supply an idempotency_key per job. Re-submitting the same key should not re-run successful sub-tasks; must be documented semantics
Retries: server will support safe retriable idempotent retries and clients should be able to re-send individual chunks with offsets
Backpressure & quotas: enforce per-customer concurrent job limits and provide explicit 429 with Retry-After when quota exceeded
Observability: Console shows job progress, per-shard throughput, and per-item failure reasons; metrics emitted (jobs_created, jobs_completed, items_processed, items_failed)
E2E test harness that simulates network flakiness and duplicate chunk submission; measured duplicate suppression rate >= 99.99%
Security review and API docs updated with examples for Node/Python, and an RFC in Confluence linked from the ticket
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API & control plane): define OpenAPI schema for /v1/embeddings/batch and /v1/embeddings/async (including idempotency_key header). Draft Confluence RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/EmbeddingsIngest-RFC
Phase 2 (job runner & storage): implement a durable job queue (use existing jobs-service with new job type 'embedding_ingest'), design S3-backed staged part storage for large uploads
Phase 3 (runtime integration): wire job runner to serving runtime with streaming KV cache writes and batch window control; add a bulk-infer path that can pull parts directly from staged storage
Phase 4 (client & docs): publish SDK helpers for chunked uploads, provide sample CLI, update console to display job progress and per-item errors
Phase 5 (hardening): add idempotency/duplication tests, canary rollout on a subset of customers, and failover behavior testing across regions
tradeoffs: We prefer eventual consistency for job visibility to keep runtime latency low; this means Console may show small delays between job completion and final metrics
Using S3-backed staged parts simplifies large-file durability but adds an extra hop and storage cost versus streaming directly to runtime; chosen for reliability and resumability

Per-item ACK semantics increase complexity (we must persist per-item status) and storage; alternative of coarse-grained job-level success was rejected due to customer needs for partial failure visibility
risks_mitigation: Risk: Duplicate vector ingestion on retries. Mitigation: canonical id per-record (client_provided id or server-generated stable id) and per-job idempotency mapping with TTL; test duplicate suppression at scale
Risk: Runtime throughput regressions under large jobs. Mitigation: throttled concurrent job execution, dynamic batch window tuning, and canary runs with traffic shaping
Risk: Cost blowup from staged parts. Mitigation: lifecycle policy to expire staged parts after 24 hours and aggregation of small parts into compressed batches before runtime consumption
Risk: Long tail latency for small synchronous batches. Mitigation: maintain separate fast-path for <= 512 records that uses in-memory streaming to runtime
testing_plan: Unit tests for job state machine and idempotency mapping (edge cases: partial success, replays)
Integration tests: end-to-end pipeline from client SDK -> jobs-service -> staged storage -> runtime -> status polling
Chaos test: simulate intermittent S3 failures and runner restarts; assert job resumes and final correctness
Load test: publish 1M items across multiple concurrent jobs in staging and validate throughput/scaling and cost-per-token telemetry
Compliance test: ensure job payloads can be configured to use customer KMS for staged parts when Private mode is used
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: RFC draft complete and posted to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/EmbeddingsIngest-RFC). Initial schema proposed for /v1/embeddings/async. PM feedback: prefer 'job_id' over 'task_id'

2026-02-25: Spike: implemented prototype uploader that writes chunked parts to S3 and returns job_id; prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-spike/pull/6

2026-03-02: Design review with Runtime team. Decided to expose a bulk-infer path that reads compressed parts directly (avoids rehydrating JSON into memory). Runtime asks for clear contract: max part size 64MB and per-item meta header
2026-03-05: Security review kickoff. Requirements for KMS integration and auditing identified; Security requested a threat model doc and key rotation plan

2026-03-09: API schema refined: added header 'Idempotency-Key' and 'X-Parts-Offset' for partial chunk upload. UX: SDK will auto-resume using part offsets. Created GitHub epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/431
2026-03-10: Began wiring jobs-service handler and adding DB table 'embedding_ingest_jobs' (migration PR opened, see: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/442).
review_feedback: Design: Console team asked for per-shard error grouping to reduce noise when thousands of items fail for the same reason
PM: requested SLA for job completion percentiles for 'small' (<=10k) and 'large' jobs; deferred to SRE for capacity estimates
Runtime: insisted on explicit backpressure control API so serving pods can reject or slow ingestion when bursty traffic impacts online latency
